audit: (1) Diagnosis labels are free-text ICD-O morphology terms with heavy overlap and many uninformative labels (missing, Unknown, 'Neoplasm, malignant', 'Glioma, malignant', 'Rhabdomyosarcoma, NOS'); 'Glioma, malignant' mixes high-grade/DIPG cases (H3 K27M, TP53, ATRX, PPM1D) with others, so frequencies per label are label-specific and may not transfer. (2) Six to ten cases are hypermutated (thousands of mutations, e.g. [case id] 15731, several 'Glioma, malignant' cases >3000, consistent with MMR/POLE deficiency); they inflate counts for large genes (ATRX, NF1, TP53, KMT2D) and I excluded cases with >100 mutations from testing. (3) Several recurrent variants look like artifacts or unfiltered germline/alternate-transcript calls across all diagnoses (C17orf80 S281R, HLTF Q898E, ZNF510 Q248E, CD69 L176Q, CD46 K388N, SLAMF7 W184R, TSPAN19 D123N, CCDC168 Q1530*, ABCF1 P9L); BRAF V600E appears as p.V640E (non-canonical transcript). (4) Four strongly 'significant' signals look implausible and were deliberately NOT claimed: PIK3R1 in Pilocytic astrocytoma (30/168), ARID1B in 'Rhabdomyosarcoma, NOS' (16/66), ZMYM3 in 'Glioma, malignant' (20/166) and ASXL1 in Medulloblastoma (17/212). Each consists of one non-recurrent, mostly missense mutation per case scattered across the whole protein (no hotspots, no domain clustering, unlike PIK3R1 iSH2 in-frame deletions seen in the high-grade gliomas), in low-burden tumors, and none matches known biology at that frequency; they look like injected or systematic artifacts, so they are a warning that the mutation table may not be fully clean. (5) Exome SNV/indel data miss the defining lesions of many tumors (KIAA1549-BRAF fusion in pilocytic astrocytoma, fusions in alveolar RMS/Ewing/synovial sarcoma, ZFTA/YAP1 fusions in ependymoma, copy-number events), so absent associations are not evidence of absence. (6) Many diagnoses have <10 cases; ~1000 diagnosis-gene tests were run, so small-n hits (e.g. CYP4F8 in large cell MB, NOS3, LEPR/VAV1 in choroid plexus carcinoma) were discarded as likely chance. Possible duplicated/related samples (identical single-mutation profiles) were not resolvable without sample metadata.
methods: For each case I marked a gene as mutated if it had >=1 non-synonymous somatic mutation. Cases with >100 mutations (hypermutators, 21 cases) were excluded from testing. For every diagnosis label and gene with >=3 mutated cases and >=2 in the diagnosis, I ran a one-sided Fisher exact (hypergeometric) test of the diagnosis versus all other cases and applied Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Significant hits were then reviewed for biological plausibility (hotspot clustering, truncating pattern for tumor suppressors, burden of carrier tumors, consistency with known pediatric tumor biology); recurrent artifact-like variants and patternless scattered-missense signals were rejected. Expected frequencies are the observed carrier fraction shrunk toward literature expectations; probabilities combine statistical strength, sample size and prior knowledge.
